value.name: Sonoma Clean Power - CleanStart
value.notes: Sonoma Clean Power's own official FAQ page (directly fetched) confirms Santa Rosa as a member city; new customers are automatically enrolled in its 'CleanStart' product (51% renewable, 91% carbon-free per the source). PG&E remains the distribution/billing utility — customers receive one combined PG&E bill showing both SCP and PG&E charges, and PG&E maintains the poles/transmission lines. Customers may opt out back to PG&E generation.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Santa Rosa/Sonoma County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC/PG&E-administered SGIP program and figures already confirmed for the San Jose/Fremont/Oakland/Fresno/Stockton records, reused on the same reasoning: SGIP is administered per IOU distribution territory (PG&E), not per city. Sonoma Clean Power may separately offer its own local storage incentives not yet researched — this field covers only the statewide SGIP program. Removed the previously-listed "SGIP - Equity Resiliency" line item on 2026-08-09: its expires_on (2025-12-31) has definitively elapsed and no renewal/replacement was confirmed this session, so it no longer represents a current program; the remaining item(s) here are still active/unknown-status per their own status field.
